_strings.@@d3b6dff18778: Treaty conformity — MO conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from MO income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the MO return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Missouri's resident return starts from federal adjusted gross income and has no treaty-exempt income add-back, so federally treaty-exempt income (already excluded from federal AGI) flows through untaxed -> conforms. Form MO-1040 Line 1 is captioned "Federal adjusted gross income," and the 2024 MO-1040 instructions state "You must begin your Missouri return with your total federal adjusted gross income, even if you have income from a state other than Missouri." The only additions to federal AGI are on Form MO-A, Part 1, Lines 1-6 (interest on state and local obligations other than Missouri source; partnership/fiduciary/S-corp/business-interest/NOL adjustments; nonqualified 529-plan distributions; Food Pantry contributions included on federal Schedule A; nonresident property tax modification; nonqualified ABLE-program distributions) — none of which add back federally treaty-exempt income or foreign-earned income. Corroborating: the "Nonresident Alien" special filing instructions direct the filer to "Enter your federal adjusted gross income from U.S. Nonresident Alien Income Tax Return (Federal Form 1040NR), Line 11, on Form MO-1040, Line 1," meaning treaty-exempt income already excluded from 1040NR AGI carries to MO Line 1 unchanged with no reattachment. Unlike California (which adds treaty income back on Schedule CA), Missouri has no analogous addback. Cite: 2024 MO-1040 Instructions, Line 1 and Form MO-A Part 1.
_strings.@@e7e97d58c856: Property Tax Credit Claim (Circuit Breaker) — Missouri residents who fall into one of four qualification categories (2024 Form MO-PTS): (A) age 65 or older and a full-year MO resident; (B) 100% disabled veteran as a result of military service; (C) 100% disabled (per SSA letter or Form SSA-1099); or (D) age 60 or older and receiving surviving spouse Social Security benefits. Available to both renters/part-year owners and full-year homeowners. Renters who rent from a facility that does not pay real estate tax are not eligible.

calls.work_head: MO state income tax (2024, graduated brackets): taxable_base $40,000.00 — which must be the state form's OWN taxable-income line, with the state's deductions/exemptions already computed on the form (this state's deduction is income-dependent or otherwise not a fixed amount the op could subtract) — with no exemptions or standard deduction to subtract; graduated tax on $40,000 [married_filing_jointly (qualifying surviving spouse uses the married-filing-jointly column) schedule]: 0 x $1,273.00 (the $0-$1,273 bracket) = $0.00; 0.02 x $1,273.00 (the $1,273-$2,546 bracket) = $25.46; 0.025 x $1,273.00 (the $2,546-$3,819 bracket) = $31.82; 0.03 x $1,273.00 (the $3,819-$5,092 bracket) = $38.19; 0.035 x $1,273.00 (the $5,092-$6,365 bracket) = $44.56; 0.04 x $1,273.00 (the $6,365-$7,638 bracket) = $50.92; 0.045 x $1,273.00 (the $7,638-$8,911 bracket) = $57.28; 0.048 x $31,089.00 (the $8,911+ bracket) = $1,492.27; total $1,740.51 -> $1,741

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form MO-1040 Line 30: 'Tax (see tax chart on page 26 of the instructions)', computed per column (30Y/30S) from Line 29Y/29S. Instructions p.26, '2024 Tax Chart': 'To identify your tax, use your Missouri taxable income from Form MO-1040, Line 29Y and 29S and the tax chart in Section A below. A separate tax must be computed for you and your spouse. ... Round to the nearest whole dollar and enter on Form MO-1040, Line 30Y and 30S.' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2024 CHANGES: the top rate fell to 4.8% (from 4.95% in 2023) and the chart's income steps re-indexed to $1,273 increments (2023: $1,207) — breakpoints $1,273 / $2,546 / $3,819 / $5,092 / $6,365 / $7,638 / $8,911; verified against BOTH the 2024 MO-1040 instructions p.26 and the 2024 MO-1040A short-form instructions p.10 (identical chart). Base guidance: Supply 2024 Form MO-1040 Line 29 'Taxable income' — one column at a time: Line 29Y (yourself) or Line 29S (spouse). Line 29 = total Missouri AGI (Line 6, which starts from federal AGI plus/minus Form MO-A adjustments) minus total deductions (Line 25: the pension/Social Security exemption; the Lines 9-13 FEDERAL INCOME TAX DEDUCTION — Line 11 federal tax x a percentage set by Missouri AGI: 35% if Line 6 is $25,000 or less, 25% for $25,001-$50,000, 15% for $50,001-$100,000, 5% for $100,001-$125,000, 0% for $125,001 or more, capped at $5,000 per individual / $10,000 combined; the Line 14 standard or itemized deduction; the Line 15 $1,400 head-of-household/qualifying-widow(er) exemption; and other deductions on Lines 16-24), apportioned by each spouse's income percentage (Line 7, applied at Line 27), minus any Line 28 enterprise-zone/rural-empowerment modification. Single, married filing separately, head of household, and qualifying widow(er) filers have one column — supply that Line 29 amount. MARRIED FILING COMBINED: Missouri taxes each spouse's column separately — run this op once with Line 29Y and once with Line 29S and add the two results (Form MO-1040 Lines 30Y + 30S); do NOT supply the couple's combined taxable income as one amount, or the tax will be overstated. One rate schedule for all filing statuses: the 2024 Tax Rate Chart (MO-1040 instructions p.26) makes no distinction by filing status, so the identical schedule is shipped for all four statuses. Qualifying widow(er) maps to married_filing_jointly here and uses the same chart. CRITICAL for married filing combined: Missouri computes tax SEPARATELY for each spouse — 'A separate tax must be computed for you and your spouse' (instructions p.26). Combined income is split by each spouse's income percentage (Line 7, applied at Line 27), producing Line 29Y and 29S, each run through the chart (Line 30Y/30S), then added. Running a couple's combined taxable income through the brackets as one amount OVERSTATES tax (a second pass through the below-4.8% brackets). Run this op once per spouse's Line 29 column and sum the results. Printed-constant rounding (quantified): the 2024 chart's flat add-on constants ($25 / $57 / $95 / $140 / $191 / $248) are rounded from the exact cumulative marginal sums ($25.46 / $57.285 / $95.475 / $140.03 / $190.95 / $248.235); the largest divergence is $0.475 at the $5,092 breakpoint. This op does exact marginal math, so its result can differ from the form worksheet's result by up to ~$1 after rounding (e.g. taxable income $12,000: exact marginal 396.507 -> 397 vs worksheet 248 + 148.27 = 396.27 -> 396; the booklet's own Example B prints 396). The filed return should use the p.26 Tax Calculation Worksheet's printed constants or the DOR online calculator at dor.mo.gov/personal/individual/. Federal income tax deduction (Missouri base quirk, NOT modeled): MO-1040 Lines 9-13 deduct Line 11 federal income tax times a Missouri-AGI-based percentage (Line 12 chart: 35% if Line 6 is $25,000 or less; 25% $25,001-$50,000; 15% $50,001-$100,000; 5% $100,001-$125,000; 0% $125,001 or more), capped at $5,000 per individual / $10,000 married filing combined. Because it is income-dependent it is not modeled — it must already be reflected in the Line 29 taxable income you supply. standard_deduction ships as null because the base is Line 29 taxable income, from which the Line 14 deduction was already subtracted — do not subtract it again. For reference, 2024 Missouri standard deductions (printed on Form MO-1040 Line 14): $14,600 single or married filing separate; $21,900 head of household; $29,200 married filing combined or qualifying widow(er). Additional standard deduction for each 65-or-older or blind condition (Line 14 instructions): $1,950 for single and head of household; $1,550 for married filing combined, married filing separate, or qualified widow(er). Itemizers use Form MO-A Part 2 instead. Head of household / qualifying widow(er) additional exemption: $1,400 on MO-1040 Line 15 (unchanged for 2024) — a base reduction already included in the Line 29 base, so it is not shipped; the Missouri filing status must match the federal filing status to claim it. The 2024 MO-1040 has NO personal or dependent exemption lines — exemptions is intentionally empty; exemptions_count and dependents_count have no effect for Missouri. Zero-rate floor: Missouri taxable income of $0 to $1,273 owes $0 (shipped as a rate-'0' bottom bracket); the state is graduated, not flat, for 2024. Rounding rule (instructions p.26 and 'Dollars and Cents': 'For 1 cent through 49 cents, round down ... For 50 cents through 99 cents, round up', with the booklet's own example 'Round $32.50 up to $33.00') — matches the engine's half-up rounding. No lookup-table mandate: Missouri publishes no tax table; all filers compute Line 30 from the Tax Rate Chart / Tax Calculation Worksheet (or the DOR online calculator). Not modeled — MO-1040 Line 34 other taxes: tax on lump-sum distributions (Federal Form 4972) and recapture of low-income housing credits (Federal Form 8611); these are added after Line 30 on the form. Not modeled — apportionment and credits after Line 30: nonresidents/part-year residents multiply Line 30 by the Missouri income percentage (Line 32, Form MO-NRI), and residents may take the resident credit for taxes paid other states (Line 31, Form MO-CR); this op produces the pre-apportionment Line 30 amount. Also not modeled (they are CREDITS against tax, not base reductions): Property Tax Credit (Line 45, MO-PTS), Missouri Working Family Tax Credit (Line 44, MO-WFTC — 20% of the federal EIC for 2024, up from 10%), and miscellaneous credits (Line 43, MO-TC). This pack follows the 2024 Form MO-1040 long form; the MO-1040A short form uses the same 2024 Tax Chart (its instructions were the second-pass source) but has its own line layout.
